title: Meet Uganda
description: Travel to Uganda with Spark and Mango: a country in Eastern Africa whose capital is Kampala, where people speak English and pay with the Ugandan shilling — plus two places we'd love to visit.

body.heading: Where in the world is Uganda?
paragraphs: Uganda is a country in Eastern Africa, which is part of Africa.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Uganda is Kampala.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Uganda speak English and Swahili.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Uganda is the Ugandan shilling.

body.heading: How big is Uganda?
paragraphs: Uganda covers about 242,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of Cameroon.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Bwindi's ancient, misty forest is home to nearly half the world's mountain gorillas. Guided treks lead families to spend an unforgettable hour with a gorilla family.
At Jinja, the River Nile begins its long journey from Lake Victoria. Families take boat rides to the spring point and watch fishermen and fish eagles.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Uganda on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Uganda in one breath: a country in Eastern Africa, capital Kampala, where people speak English and pay with the Ugandan shilling.
materials: A globe, atlas or world map (to find Uganda)
Paper and crayons or pencils for the screen-free mission
supervision: Read this one together: a grown-up can help with tricky place names and hunt for Uganda on the map as you read.
